title: Aurum Alpha subscription, ledger, override and entitlement decision
description: The shapes of standards/075-billing.md BL2 and BL4: the subscription projection, the append-only ledger row, the override, the decision the check returns, the derived entitlement set that feeds /me (060 AU6), and the extension members the entitlement-required problem carries inside 050 HA3's envelope. This file fixes the model; contracts/billing/entitlements.json fixes the behaviour. Ids and timestamps are $refs into the identifiers contract, never restated. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

status.description: BL2: the closed status set. BL4's policy maps each to what the plan contributes: trialing and active the full plan; past_due the full plan for the catalog's grace period, then the suspended set; cancelled the suspended set, the row having taken effect at period end.

ledgerKind.description: BL2: the closed set of transitions. A sign-up onto a paid plan with no trial is upgraded from no plan; an expired trial is a cancellation that never paid. A kind outside this set is a schema failure, not a new row.

actorType.description: BL2: the closed set of actors. Maps to 080 AE2's actor.type as user, user, service and system respectively (BL10).

actor.description: BL2: who caused the row. For user and internal_admin the id is the application's own public id for the person (IP1); for job the job's name; for provider_webhook the provider's source name as 055 AM8 re-envelopes it.

planRef.description: BL1: a plan id from the catalog, or null for no plan — before the first row, and after a cancellation has taken effect.

entitlementId.description: BL3: a capability, metric or setting id. snake_case, no dot.

pendingChange.description: BL2: the one change scheduled to take effect later, derived from the single ledger row whose effective_at is still in the future. There is no array of these: a second pending change is a schema failure, and a row recorded while one is pending supersedes it.

kind.description: BL7: only a downgrade or a cancellation waits for period end. An upgrade and a reactivation take effect at recording.

ledger_id.description: BL2: the row this pending change is. A pending change is never anything but a row.

subscription.description: BL2: the projection, one per tenant, written only by applying a ledger row — except the period boundaries, which mirror the provider's events because the period is when the provider charges (BL6). It is the current answer; the ledger is the truth.

tenant_id.description: BL3: entitlements attach to the tenant and to nothing smaller. There is no user_id here and never will be.

current_period_end.description: BL2, BL7: the instant a pending downgrade or cancellation takes effect and the instant an allowance resets (BL3).

trial_end.description: BL8: when the trial ends; null when there is none or it has ended. The trial.expire job reads it; the banner reads it; the function already knows it.

catalog_version.description: BL1: the catalog version the tenant is priced under. Prices are grandfathered by this; entitlements are always the current catalog's.

provider.description: BL5, BL9: the provider's ids for this tenant, absent until the provider confirms them, because the local transaction commits before the boundary call is acknowledged.

last_ledger_id.description: BL4: the most recently recorded row, one third of the entitlement cache key. Every row changes it, so every row invalidates by construction.

ledgerRow.description: BL2: one transition, append-only. The service's grant on this table carries INSERT and SELECT and nothing else (080 AE6's discipline). A correction is a new row with a reason. Every row also emits an audit event in the same transaction (BL10).

recorded_at.description: BL2: when the row was written. Rows are applied in this order.

effective_at.description: BL2: when the transition takes effect. Equal to recorded_at for an immediate change; later for a downgrade or cancellation at period end, which makes the row the pending change until then. The function of BL4 applies a row only once 'at' has reached this instant, which is what lets it answer for any date.

from_status.description: BL2: null only on a tenant's first row.

catalog_version.description: BL1: the catalog version this change was priced under — grandfathered pricing without a mechanism.

provider_event_id.description: BL6: the provider's event id where a webhook caused the row, unique per tenant, so a redelivered event is a repeat under 055 AM3 and never a second row. Null for rows the product or a person originated.

override_id.description: BL2: the override an override_granted or override_revoked row concerns. Null for every other kind.

reason.description: BL7, BL10: the justification an internal administrator gave. Required by review on every internal_admin row; carried to the audit event's reason.

override.description: BL2: one adjustment to one entitlement for one tenant, granted by an internal administrator with a 070 permission and written as an override_granted ledger row. It applies from granted_at until expires_at or revoked_at, at any status (BL4). There is no user-level override: a per-user grant is a permission (BL3).

kind.description: BL3: which of the four kinds the target is.

value.description: BL4: the effective value while the override lives — true for a capability granted, a ceiling or null for a quota or allowance, the setting's value for a setting. Where the plan also speaks, this wins.

reason.description: BL7: why. Required, because an override with no reason is a comp nobody can explain on the audit trail.

granted_by.description: BL10: the administrator's public id; the audit event's actor.

expires_at.description: BL4: the instant after which the override contributes nothing. Null admits an open-ended override and is the review question on every grant.

revoked_at.description: BL2: set by an override_revoked row. The override row is not deleted; the ledger explains it.

reason.description: BL4: why the decision came out as it did — which plan or which override decided, or that the suspended set applied. Present on every decision, allowed or not, because a denial has to say which plan refused so the problem envelope can name it.

source.description: BL4: plan when the plan's own definition decided; override when an override did; suspended when the status policy replaced the plan with the suspended set.

id.description: BL4: the plan id, the override's public id, or the status (past_due or cancelled) that caused suspension.

decision.description: BL4: what entitled, withinQuota and withinAllowance return. Never a bare boolean, for 070 RB8's reason. The reason is logged and shown to an administrator; the caller receives the entitlement-required problem, which names the plan and the entitlement and nothing else.

sourcedValue.description: BL4: a quota, allowance or setting value with the source that decided it.

sourcedAllowance.description: BL3, BL4: an allowance value with the period it resets on, taken from the subscription's current period.

entitlementSet.description: BL4: the derived set for one tenant at one instant — never stored, the output of entitlementsFor. The same shape is the 'entitlements' block of the /me document (060 AU6), advisory there exactly as 'permissions' is: the server enforces on every request.

suspended.description: BL4: whether the status policy replaced the plan's contribution with the suspended set at 'at'.

catalog_version.description: BL1, BL4: the version of the catalog the set was derived from — the current one, not the version the tenant is priced under. Entitlements are current; prices are grandfathered. One third of the cache key.

capabilities.description: BL4: the true, complete, sorted list of capabilities the tenant holds at 'at', from the plan's contribution and live overrides together.

pending_change.description: BL7: so the client can say 'moves to team on the 20th' without a second request.

valid_until.description: BL4: the earliest instant after 'at' at which this set would differ with no new ledger row — a grace period ending, a period ending, a trial ending, an override expiring, a pending row taking effect. Null when none is known. A cache honours it; a cache keyed on the ledger alone serves a plan through the end of its grace period.

entitlementRequired.description: BL4: the entitlement-required response, which is 050 HA3's problem+json envelope (contracts/http/problem.schema.json) with two extension members, 'entitlement' and 'plan', as RFC 9457 admits. Every member the envelope requires is required here with the meaning HA3 gives it; this def narrows type and status and adds the two members, and nothing else may appear. Not 402: RFC 9110 reserves it and intermediaries mishandle it; HA3 makes type, not status, the thing a client branches on.

type.description: HA3: the portfolio form, with the service's own segment.

title.description: HA3: the same string for every instance of this type.

detail.description: HA3: this occurrence's reason — which plan, which entitlement, which limit. Never the person's grants (070 RB8).

instance.description: HA3: the request path, where one exists.

entitlement.description: BL4: what was missing. A statement about the tenant, not the person, which is why it may cross the boundary where 070 RB8's reason does not.

limit.description: BL3: the ceiling that was reached, for a quota or allowance. Absent for a capability.

plan.description: BL4: the tenant's current plan, so the client can render which plan would satisfy the request. Null when the tenant has none.
